propositions: The AC1 equivalence contract in test_operation_snapshot_surfaces.py was vacuous because MCP and reconciler blocks re-called the shared composer rather than invoking real entry points, making it impossible to catch parity bugs if those surfaces stopped routing through the composer.

The real MCP surface must be driven via build_server() and call_tool() on explain_criterion to verify it routes through compose_operation_snapshot via the module-global binding in emit_shadow_snapshot.
The real reconciler surface must be driven via rebar_reconciler.__main__.main() with --dry-run-enumerate to verify it routes through _emit_operation_shadow before any lock, pass, or network effect.

Each surface's composed snapshot must be anchored to absolute expected content (repo root, envelope version, config keys with verified provenance) in addition to cross-surface equality, so composer perturbations are caught rather than moving all surfaces together.

The recorder capturing compose_operation_snapshot calls must fire for each surface (guarded by an explicit assertion), preventing the failure mode where a spy that never fires is indistinguishable from a passing assertion.
